title: ContextActionService
summary: Client-side action binding that works across devices: BindAction gives one handler for keyboard, gamepad, and auto-generated touch buttons — the cross-platform input layer.

methods.name: BindAction
methods.signature: ContextActionService:BindAction(actionName: string, functionToBind: (actionName, inputState, inputObject) -> Enum.ContextActionResult?, createTouchButton: boolean, ...inputs: Enum.KeyCode | Enum.UserInputType)
methods.description: Binds an action to one or more inputs; optionally creates a mobile touch button. Handler receives (actionName, Enum.UserInputState, inputObject).

methods.name: UnbindAction
methods.description: Removes the binding and its touch button.

details.heading: Handler lifecycle
details.body: Your handler fires for Begin AND End input states — check `inputState == Enum.UserInputState.Begin` for press actions. Return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink to consume the input, Handled otherwise.

explanation.whatItIs: 'Bind the concept of an action' instead of raw keys: you define 'Reload', CAS routes keyboard keys, gamepad buttons, AND a generated touch button into one handler.
explanation.whyItExists: Shipping to PC + console + mobile with raw UserInputService means three input paths per action. CAS unifies them.
whenToUse: Gameplay actions that should work on every platform (dash, reload, interact)
When mobile users need an auto-generated button with zero extra UI work
When you need to bind/unbind actions dynamically per game state
whenNotToUse: For low-level needs (mouse position, raw deltas, continuous values) — use UserInputService
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
BindAction("Dash", onDash, true,
    Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift,           -- keyboard
    Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL2)            -- gamepad

Mobile players automatically get a
'Dash' touch button on screen.

onDash(actionName, inputState, inputObject)
    └─ check inputState == Begin
```
tips: Return ContextActionResult.Sink when you handled it so lower-priority bindings don't also fire
Unbind when the context disappears (menus, cinematics)
Style the touch button (SetTitle/SetImage/SetPosition/BindActivate) for polished mobile UX
commonMistakes: Acting on both Begin and End states — guard with inputState == Begin
Forgetting the createTouchButton flag and wondering why mobile has no button
Binding the same action name twice — the second overwrites the first

examples.title: Cross-platform dash action
examples.code:
local ContextActionService = game:GetService("ContextActionService")

local function onDash(actionName, inputState, inputObject)
    if inputState ~= Enum.UserInputState.Begin then return end
    print("Dashing!")
    return Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink
end

ContextActionService:BindAction(
    "Dash",
    onDash,
    true,                              -- create touch button for mobile
    Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift,            -- keyboard
    Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL2              -- gamepad
)

ContextActionService:SetTitle("Dash", "DASH")

-- Later (e.g. during a cutscene):
-- ContextActionService:UnbindAction("Dash")
